data.narrative:
Climeworks, a Series F climate and energy company founded by Christoph Gebald and Jan Wurzbacher, has raised over $1.0B to date. The valuation analysis draws from a fragmented peer set comprising one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. The narrow Climate & Energy sector offers limited direct comparables at equivalent stage and valuation tier, constraining peer-median methodology applicability.

Stage-progression analysis provides the primary quantitative anchor. Using the $1.0B total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series F step-up multiplier of 1.3x yields an implied valuation of $1.3B. This method is applicable given Climeworks' progression through multiple funding rounds and materiality of capital deployed. Peer-median analysis was deemed inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables—only one same-stage peer was identified, below the three-datapoint threshold needed for robust median estimation.

The triangulation range is $1.1B (low) to $1.5B (median $1.3B), supported by a single methodological pillar. Key uncertainties include the limited precision of stage-based multiples absent comparable transaction data at this valuation tier and the absence of sufficiently sized peer cohorts in the climate-tech sector. Validation of this range would benefit from direct revenue multiples or deployment/capacity metrics if available.
